recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If HL7 wants to repair the historical STU3 page or the http://hl7.org/fhir/ig-publisher redirect, handle that through published-site/archive deployment rather than current FHIR source.
issue_request: FHIR-15834 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request for the STU3 downloads page IGPublisher link. The description proposed a version-local STU3 jar URL, but the later editor comment clarified that the intended target was build.fhir.org/current build.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-15834. Source history shows non-keyed downloads-page changes after the Jira decision, including 06915efa replacing the local org.hl7.fhir.igpublisher.jar link with a latest publisher CLI artifact URL.
additional_context: The current checkout builds R6 ballot content. source/downloads.html is active through source/hierarchy.xml and publish.ini, but it no longer has a direct IG Publisher jar link; it only points to the FHIR Tools Registry and notes that tools such as the IG publisher use NPM packages. Later FHIR-31735 history removed direct Validator and IG Publisher tool links from the specification downloads page. The static STU3 publication still has its own IG Publisher row and is outside the active current build source.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Editing current R6 source/downloads.html would not update the STU3 publication named by the issue and would work against later source history that split tool downloads out of the spec page.

related_jiras.note: The 2022 split-tools-out-of-spec change removed direct Validator and IG Publisher download links from the current downloads source.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive STU3 downloads-page issue about the IGPublisher link, with a later editor comment saying the link should point to build.fhir.org/current build.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes final issue scope as a historical STU3 tool-link correction rather than a current R6 source requirement.

evidence_items.summary: The active R6 downloads page is in build scope and no longer contains a direct IG Publisher jar link; it points to the FHIR Tools Registry and says tools such as the IG publisher use NPM packages.
evidence_items.learned: There is no active current-source link matching the historical STU3 problem to edit.

evidence_items.summary: History first moved the downloads-page IG Publisher link away from a version-local jar and later removed direct Validator/IG Publisher tool links under FHIR-31735.
evidence_items.learned: Later source history supports not adding a direct IG Publisher jar link back to the current downloads page.

evidence_items.learned: Any remaining repair is for the historical published page or redirect, which is outside the active R6 build source.
